angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G), matched to the same NFL route families and tested against season separation over expected (SOE) on held-out draft classes. Positive use: last season's route-shrunk SOE as a tiebreaker for day-3 and undrafted receivers, scored leave-one-season-out against a pick-and-routes forecast.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill and Combine year, averaged over route drills and shrunk for reliability. The same code runs on NFL snaps of the same route families.
headline_number: Pre-specified primary (round-9 plain forecast as an offset, one model, one interval): -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G, 90% interval -3.6 to +1.0 (n=116 on unseen classes). Day-3/UDFA, leave-one-season-out (20 pairs, 16 receivers): adding shrunk last-season SOE to pick and routes raises the held-out rank correlation from 0.06 to 0.37 (gain +0.31 [-0.08, +0.63], ahead in 88% of receiver resamples, 1 of 2 folds) and cuts RMSE by 1.2 in [-0.1, +2.3]. The yes/no list nearly ties: 7/13 vs 6/13. All rounds (53 pairs, secondary): gain +0.33 [0.13, 0.53], 2 of 2 folds.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_14/cand_2. Numbers: numbers.json rebuilt from scratch with one key per quoted number (1,225 keys down to 210). claims.json maps each key to its claim, and writeup/check.py verifies every value appears in the text. Unquoted results go to unquoted_numbers.json and figure-only values to figure_numbers.json. The stale prim_in, price_bg 9/14, tprr and ho_* keys are gone, and the only price quoted is 9% [2, 17], matching Fig 3. Primary: the plain/ridge average and the Bayesian posterior are cut. The primary is now the single forecast frozen in round 9; ridge, no-Nacua, route-mix and QB versions are sensitivity rows. Shortlist: empirical-Bayes SOE shrunk by routes (skill variance from season-to-season covariance; k=0.60 at 200 routes). Yes/no cut-off chosen on the other season pair (Youden). Continuous leave-one-season-out evaluation (rank correlation, RMSE, Brier) against pick and routes on all 53 pairs and the day-3 subset, with receiver-clustered intervals. Player-level P(2026 SOE>0) for all 13 names, with the pick-and-routes probability alongside. Title and lede state the tie. 3-row hit table; 2026 table and the Boutte/Bond disagreement cases lead the section. Drill to tape: within-family links (slant/out/hitch) with per-family drill and NFL reliability; slot/wide and man/zone slices; Bayesian errors-in-variables Bayes factor (2.8:1 for no link; P(true link >= 0.5)=6%). The text says plainly that 40 sampled plays cannot test the link. Ceiling, random band and disattenuated interval removed. Writeup: two-sentence lede, one-sentence metric, methods moved to the appendix, one-sentence captions, softened action 1. Viz: Fig 1 shows six receivers chosen by a stated rule (3 largest falls and 3 largest rises from drill to NFL), drill and NFL paths of the same route family side by side, solid blue/vermillion medians over grey reps, a 4-number readout (Break G, brake, speed through, drive), a dumbbell with bootstrap whiskers, and 10 pt footnotes. Fig 2 has the legend outside, one number per panel, and a slice forest. Fig 3 is a price/value forest with shared rows and a labelled +3 in line. Fig 4 is a day-3 strip (hit/miss, ordered by shrunk SOE, both lists marked, repeat receivers flagged) with paired held-out gains; the all-rounds result is greyed as secondary. Graft from cand_1: share of resamples where the rule wins and folds won.
open_risks: Headline is a bounded null: gains above +1.0 in per sd are excluded, losses down to -3.6 are not
Day-3 gain of last-season SOE over pick and routes is not proven: interval [-0.08, +0.63], only 1 of 2 folds, 20 pairs from 16 receivers; the yes/no list nearly ties (7/13 vs 6/13)
The two season folds pick different cut-offs (+0.5 in and -0.7 in), so the yes/no threshold is unstable; all 13 names on the 2026 list clear the cut-off fitted on both pairs
Shrinkage assumes skill is stable across consecutive seasons; the skill variance comes from 76 season pairs
Per-family NFL reliability is 0.00 to 0.40, so the drill-to-game slices (including the negative man-coverage row) are mostly noise
Game tracking is a 40-play sample per player, half selected for high EPA; the earlier rounds saw all three classes, so the 2026 class is the first blind test
